messages:
anna: Quick sync — we need to lock down the roadmap for the external action schema surface. Multiple customers asked for a stable 'results' envelope and typed schemas. Can we list launch criteria and what to prioritize for v1?

mike: Two parallel priorities IMO: 1) Enterprise-grade strict schemas + validation, 2) Lightweight flexible schema for PLG. Both should share a compat story.

sarah: Agree. For enterprise we must guarantee backward compatibility and a clear migration path. Also they want signed schema versions and explicit deprecation windows.

jess: Proposed launch checklist (short):
- schema v1 spec (JSON Schema + versioning rules)
- SDK support (py/ts) for schema validation + auto types
- runtime error contract (error codes + retry advice)
- streaming partial-results shape defined
- telemetry (schema usage, validation failures, fallback rates)
- migration docs + sample migrations

oliver: +1. Also we need test harnesses for customers: small CLI to run their prompts/requests against candidate models and report schema conformance. That will surface real regressions.

anna: Good list. For prioritization, what are the must-haves for GA vs. post-GA? My suggestion: Must-have for GA = schema v1, SDK validators, error contract, telemetry baseline, migration docs. Post-GA = signed schema registry, advanced policy routing, per-route schema overrides.

mike: That feels sensible. Also decide policy for schema strictness by route. Default should be permissive with opt-in strict mode. Many PLG apps will break on strict by default.

sarah: We should support a "compatibility mode" header so clients can opt into strict validation per call, e.g. `X-Action-Schema: schema@v1+strict` so we don't force global changes.

jess: On the results envelope shape, propose:
```
{
  "action_id": "string",
  "schema_version": "string",
  "result": { "type": "object|string|array", "payload": ... },
  "metadata": { "latency_ms": number, "model": "model-name" },
  "errors": [ { "code": "string", "message": "string", "recoverable": bool } ]
}
```
This keeps a predictable top-level while letting payloads vary.

oliver: Need to call out partial/streaming semantics: partial chunks should include `schema_version` and an incremental `result_chunk_id`. Otherwise it's a mess for SDKs.

anna: Launch criteria addition: we must have fallbacks defined — if schema validation fails, what do we surface to the customer? Options: sandboxed fallback model, best-effort normalization, or explicit error. Default should be: deliver best-effort result + telemetry and an error code.

mike: Important: telemetry fields. We should capture schema_id, validation_result (pass/warn/fail), fallback_taken (bool), and latency buckets. That lets Optimize give suggestions later.

jess: Customer asks we've heard: enterprise wants deterministic enums + strict typing; startups want flexible `any`-friendly payloads and ability to evolve quickly. So the product should support both via versioned schemas and per-route toggles.

troy-bot: deploybot: New branch `action-schema/v1-spec` created and CI tests added for schema linting :rocket:.

anna: Nice. Next steps: team owners -> assign owners for SDK, runtime validation, telemetry, docs. I'll compile this into a spec doc and share for review by EOD tomorrow. If anyone thinks something is missing from GA checklist, drop a note here.

mike: Add regression tests for model-output shuffling (same prompt with different models should maintain schema shape).

sarah: Also add security review for serialized payloads. We need to ensure we don't accidentally allow arbitrary code execution in clients that auto-deserialize.

jess: +1 security. We'll include safe deserialization examples in SDKs and docs.

anna: Thanks all — I'll post the draft spec once owners are assigned.
